GraphService（C#）

Service introduction

GraphService is the service responsible for the complete life cycle management of the main image in Atom SDK. It provides a complete set of interfaces for graph creation, copying, deleting, importing (LoadGraph), exporting (ExportGraph), opening, releasing, running, clearing, timestamp management, and node information query. All methods are asynchronous, returning Task<JsonElement> (original JSON) or a concrete strongly typed model.

namespace: AtomSdk.Services

Entrance: client.Graph

Applicable scenarios

  • Create, copy, and delete diagrams in editor mode;

  • Import the local .atom file into the server (LoadGraphAsync);

  • Export graphs to files for backup or migration (ExportGraphAsync);

  • After opening the graph, edit the nodes, and finally trigger execution through RunGraphAsync;

  • Obtain and maintain graph timestamps (for consistency checking).

Recommended calling order

CreateGraphAsync          (Create a new picture)
        ↓
OpenGraphAsync            (open diagram,Get timestamp)
        ↓
[Use NodeService Edit node]
        ↓
RunGraphAsync             (Run chart,Polling waiting for completion)
        ↓
ReleaseGraphAsync         (Release resources)

Interface detailed explanation

CreateGraphAsync(…​)

// original JsonElement version
Task<JsonElement> CreateGraphAsync(
    CreateGraphParams paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

// Generic version(Automatically deserialize to specified type)
Task<T> CreateGraphAsync<T>(
    CreateGraphParams paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

// Strongly typed convenience version
Task<GraphReference> CreateGraphInfoAsync(
    CreateGraphParams paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

Purpose: Create a new main image on the Atom platform.

Parameters

Name type Description

paramsData.GraphName

string

Picture name, unique within the platform

paramsData.Description

string?

Description of the graph, optional, defaults to null

cancellationToken

CancellationToken

Cancellation token, optional

Return value: Task<JsonElement>, key fields:

field type Description

graphId

string

The unique ID of the newly created graph

graphName

string

Picture name

timestamp

double

Creation timestamp

example

using System;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using AtomSdk;
using AtomSdk.Models;

var client = new AtomClient("http://localhost:8080");

// Method one:original JsonElement
var raw = await client.Graph.CreateGraphAsync(
    new CreateGraphParams("detection_graph", "Target detection pipeline"));
string graphId = raw.GetProperty("graphId").GetString()!;
Console.WriteLine($"Created successfully,Figure ID: {graphId}");
Console.WriteLine($"Request status: {raw.GetProperty("status").GetInt32()}");

// Method 2:Strongly typed model(Recommended)
var info = await client.Graph.CreateGraphInfoAsync(new CreateGraphParams("detection_graph"));
Console.WriteLine($"Figure ID: {info.GraphId},Picture title: {info.GraphName}");
Console.WriteLine($"Request status: {info.Status}");

ListGraphsAsync(…​)

// original JsonElement version

    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

// Generic version
Task<T> ListGraphsAsync<T>(
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

// Strongly typed convenience version
Task<GraphSummary[]> ListGraphSummariesAsync(
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

Purpose: Get a list summary of all images on the platform (excluding thumbnails).

Parameters

Name type Description

cancellationToken

CancellationToken

Cancellation token, optional

Return value: Task<JsonElement>, which is an array, each element contains the basic information of the graph (graphName, graphId, etc.).

example

using System;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using AtomSdk;

var client = new AtomClient("http://localhost:8080");

// original version:Traverse JsonElement array
var raw = await client.Graph.ListGraphsAsync();
foreach (var item in raw.EnumerateArray())
{
    Console.WriteLine(item.GetProperty("graphName").GetString());
}

// Strongly typed version
var summaries = await client.Graph.ListGraphSummariesAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"share {summaries.Length} pictures");
foreach (var s in summaries)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"- {s.GraphName} ({s.GraphId})");
}

LoadGraphAsync(…​)

// original JsonElement version
Task<JsonElement> LoadGraphAsync(
    LoadGraphParams paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

// Generic version
Task<T> LoadGraphAsync<T>(
    LoadGraphParams paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

// Strongly typed convenience version
Task<GraphLoadResult> LoadGraphResultAsync(
    LoadGraphParams paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

Purpose: Upload and import this map file (.atom format) to the Atom platform and transmit it in multipart/form-data mode. Before importing, SDK will first read the current graph list; if paramsData.GraphName already exists, InvalidOperationException will be thrown, /Graph/LoadGraph will not be called, and the existing graph will not be overwritten. You need to use a new graph name or delete the existing graph and try again.

Parameters

Name type Description

paramsData.GraphName

string

The name of the image on the platform after importing

paramsData.FilePath

string

Absolute or relative path to local file

cancellationToken

CancellationToken

Cancellation token, optional

Return value: Task<JsonElement>, import result information (graphId, graphName).

example

using System;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using AtomSdk;

var client = new AtomClient("http://localhost:8080");

var result = await client.Graph.LoadGraphResultAsync(
    new LoadGraphParams("imported_graph", "/data/graphs/my_pipeline.atom"));
Console.WriteLine($"Import successful,Figure ID: {result.GraphId}");
Console.WriteLine($"Request status: {result.Status}");

ImportExtensionNodesByPathAsync(…​)

// original JsonElement version
Task<JsonElement> ImportExtensionNodesByPathAsync(
    ImportExtensionNodesByPathParams paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

// Generic version
Task<T> ImportExtensionNodesByPathAsync<T>(
    ImportExtensionNodesByPathParams paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

Purpose: Import the extended node file decompressed by LoadGraphAsync. This interface is usually Called after LoadGraphAsync, the parameters are passed in LoadGraphAsync in the return value ExtensionNodes field, do not pass the entire LoadGraphAsync return object.

Parameters

Name type Description

paramsData.ExtensionNodes

JsonElement or IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?>

LoadGraphAsync The ExtensionNodes field in the return value

cancellationToken

CancellationToken

Cancellation token, optional

example

var loadResult = await client.Graph.LoadGraphResultAsync(
    new LoadGraphParams("imported_graph", "/data/graphs/my_pipeline.atom"));

if (loadResult.ExtensionNodes.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object &&
    loadResult.ExtensionNodes.EnumerateObject().Any())
{
    var importResult = await client.Graph.ImportExtensionNodesByPathAsync(
        new ImportExtensionNodesByPathParams(loadResult.ExtensionNodes));
    Console.WriteLine(importResult);
}

};
var exportResult = await client.Graph.ExportGraphAsync(new ExportGraphParams("my_graph", dlModels));

RunGraphAsync(…​)

// original JsonElement version
Task<JsonElement> RunGraphAsync(
    string graphName,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default,
    TimeSpan? timeout = null)

// Generic version
Task<T> RunGraphAsync<T>(
    string graphName,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default,
    TimeSpan? timeout = null)

// Strongly typed convenience version
Task<GraphRunResult> RunGraphResultAsync(
    string graphName,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default,
    TimeSpan? timeout = null)

Purpose: Trigger a complete run of the specified graph. SDK will poll internally until the result is returned after the run is completed. The default wait is up to 30 seconds; if it exceeds timeout, AtomTimeoutException is thrown, and the exception contains the last response.

Parameters

Name type Description

graphName

string

Picture name

cancellationToken

CancellationToken

Cancellation token, used by the caller to actively cancel

timeout

TimeSpan?

SDK polling wait timeout; null uses the default 30 seconds, Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan means waiting forever

Return value: Task<JsonElement>, the result data after the operation is completed, including the value of each output port.

example

using System;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using AtomSdk;

var client = new AtomClient("http://localhost:8080");

var result = await client.Graph.RunGraphResultAsync(
    "my_graph",
    timeout: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(60));
Console.WriteLine($"Run completed,Request status: {result.Status}");

Complete business process example

The following example demonstrates the complete editor flow from creating a graph to running it:

using System;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using AtomSdk;
using AtomSdk.Core;

class GraphWorkflowExample
{
    static async Task Main()
    {
        var client = new AtomClient("http://localhost:8080");
        const string graphName = "my_pipeline";

        try
        {
            // 1. Create diagram
            var graphInfo = await client.Graph.CreateGraphInfoAsync(graphName, "Image processing pipeline");
            Console.WriteLine($"[1] Diagram created: {graphInfo.GraphId}, Request status: {graphInfo.Status}");

            // 2. List all pictures,Confirm creation is successful
            var summaries = await client.Graph.ListGraphSummariesAsync();
            Console.WriteLine($"[2] Current number of pictures: {summaries.Length}");

            // 3. open diagram(Get timestamp,Subsequent edits require timestamps)
            await client.Graph.OpenGraphAsync(graphName);
            Console.WriteLine("[3] Image is open");

            // 4. Create nodes in the graph(Use NodeService)
            var node1 = await client.Node.CreateNodeInfoAsync(graphName, "ResizeImage");
            var node2 = await client.Node.CreateNodeInfoAsync(graphName, "DetectAndSegment");
            Console.WriteLine($"[4] Created 2 nodes: {node1.NodeId}, {node2.NodeId}, Request status={node2.Status}");

            // 5. Connect nodes
            await client.Node.ConnectNodesAsync(
                graphName,
                inputNodeId: node2.NodeId, inputPortName: "image",
                outputNodeId: node1.NodeId, outputPortName: "resized_image");
            Console.WriteLine("[5] Node is connected");

            // 6. Run chart,most wait 30 seconds
            var runResult = await client.Graph.RunGraphResultAsync(
                graphName,
                timeout: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));
            Console.WriteLine($"[6] Run completed,Request status: {runResult.Status}");

            // 7. Export graph
            var exportResult = await client.Graph.ExportGraphResultAsync(graphName);
            Console.WriteLine($"[7] Figure has been exported: {exportResult.FilePath}");

            // 8. release chart
            await client.Graph.ReleaseGraphAsync(graphName);
            Console.WriteLine("[8] Image has been released");
        }
        catch (AtomApiException ex)
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"Server error {ex.Status}: {ex.Message}");
        }
        catch (AtomHttpException ex)
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"HTTP Error {ex.StatusCode}: {ex.Message}");
        }
    }
}
